newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TCV announces operating surplus A$39.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TCV announces operating surplus A$39.1 mln.

text.p: Treasury Corporation of Victoria (TCV) said on Tuesday it had achieved a net operating surplus of A$39.1 million in the year ended June 30, 1996.
It said it would pay the state of Victoria a dividend of $25.5 million.
TCV is the financing arm of the state government of Victoria.
TCV's results were tabled in the Victoria state parliament on Tuesday by state Treasurer Alan Stockdale.

TCV managing director David Carruthers said the corporation's results were highly satisfactory given the reduced borrowing programme in 1995/96, significant changes to the client base and dealing with the complexities of the government's privatisation programme.
TCV's report confirmed that a total of A$9.9 billion of gross debt had been retired during the year, including A$1.6 billion on behalf of the State Electricity Commission of Victoria shell.
"The outcome had been a fundamental change to the balance sheet with a 25 percent reduction in gross debt from A$33.4 billion to A$25.1 billion by 30 June," TCV said.
It said it was also active in offshore markets, especially the Japanese market, earlier in the year, raising A$1.85 billion through six issues.
Since June 30, 1996, TCV said it had received the A$2.35 billion sale proceeds for Hazelwood Power Corporation.
These funds have been applied to debt maturities and early retirement to leave around A$1 billion of surplus liquid assets at September 30.
TCV was due on Wednesday to hold a tender to establish a new benchmark hot stock maturing August 2008 with a semi-annual coupon of 7.50 percent.
TCV said that for a period immediately following the tender the bond would be available via switches at mid market from other TCV hot stocks.
